paragraphs: He reports R' Yitzchak in Gittin 38a. At 43b, however, the reading is Rav Huna bar R' Katina, while Yevamot 26a reads Rav Acha bar Katina.[^1][^2]

notes.text: The exact Davidson Gittin 43b paragraph has רב הונא בר קטינא אמר רבי יצחק, supporting Rav Huna as the ר״ה name/title reading there. Hyman’s בר״ק has a father-title component rendered R' Katina, while the named witness has untitled Katina; the difference remains explicit, not silently deleted or expanded from the heading’s Rav. The distinct 38a Yitzchak occurrence remains R', since 43b’s title is not transferred to a separately cited occurrence. Earlier notes’ guess that initials presumably match Chanina is superseded by actual Huna evidence.

לח./מג:/כו. give 38a/43b/26a conventionally; there continues Gittin. The heading has full Rav twice; the Yevamot reading full Rav before Acha only, without adding title to Katina. The opening is a transmitted dictum, not Yitzchak commenting on textual readings.
